tagline: A river road became Washington’s first scenic byway, with room to slow down
intro: The Yakima River Canyon Scenic Byway follows the river’s bends beneath basalt cliffs between Ellensburg and Selah. Two lanes run along the canyon bottom, with shoulders only in places. State of Washington Tourism allows one hour for its 27-mile scenic trip. Designated in 1967 as Washington’s first scenic byway, the corridor was proposed, Governor Daniel J. Evans explained, to let travelers appreciate the landscape at a slower pace.

The state completed the canyon road in 1924 to replace a gravel route over the mountains to the west. Crews blasted tunnels through basalt; when traffic outgrew them, a new alignment closer to the river bypassed the tunnels in 1963. I-82 later diverted through traffic, and US 97 moved onto the interstate in 1973, leaving the canyon road as SR 821. The canyon highway had joined the federal US 97 route in 1926 and received concrete paving in 1932, before the narrow tunnels were bypassed.

Driving south from the Kittitas Valley, enter the canyon through hairpin turns in its narrowest stretch, then reach the footbridge at Umtanum Creek. Continue along the river to Roza Dam, where the highway stays uphill while the railroad crosses the water. Beyond the canyon’s passage through Umtanum Ridge, farms near Pomona lead toward Selah.

moments.title: Umtanum Creek Recreation Area
moments.text: A footbridge across the Yakima River connects the Umtanum Creek parking area with a network of hiking trails. It is one of five developed recreation sites managed by the Bureau of Land Management in the canyon. Here the road journey has a pedestrian crossing of its own, linking the highway side to trails across the water.

moments.title: Roza Dam
moments.text: At Roza Dam, road and railroad take different sides of the river: the railway crosses west while SR 821 remains uphill. The diversion dam was built in 1939, with a crest 486 feet long and a height of 67 feet. Power generation came online in 1956. Its adult fish ladder leads to a trap where fish are counted before release above the dam. Some wild fish are collected weekly as broodstock for the Cle Elum Supplementation and Research Facility. The dam lies just west of SR 821, making this a meeting of highway, railway and river infrastructure.

moments.title: Umtanum Ridge
moments.text: Near the canyon’s southern end, the Yakima River cuts through Umtanum Ridge. This long ridge belongs to the Yakima Fold Belt, where Miocene Columbia River basalt flows were folded into east-trending ridges. The river’s crossing is called the Umtanum Ridge Water Gap. Manastash Ridge parallels it to the north, and Yakima Ridge lies to the south.
